contextual.summary: Surrey gives UK home students who meet its contextual criteria an offer typically two A-level grades lower, and runs In2Surrey, a separate scheme that can give an offer typically one A-level grade lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: typically two A-level grades (or one BTEC grade) lower than the published grade; through In2Surrey, typically one A-level grade lower. Subject requirements are not reduced

criteria.detail: Automatic contextual offer: you live in an area where few people go on to higher education (POLAR4 quintile 1)
Automatic contextual offer: you live in an area of multiple deprivation (Indices of Multiple Deprivation, IMD quintile 1; the page says this means deciles 1 and 2)
Automatic contextual offer: you have experience of living in care (for example foster care, a children's home, a supervision order at home or kinship care)
Automatic contextual offer: you received free school meals at any point during secondary school
Automatic contextual offer: you are under 25 and estranged from your parents (not in contact with and supported by them)

Disability or long-term health condition: it is in the page's contextual data table, but not in its 'Am I eligible?' list, so it is not clear whether it alone triggers the automatic offer (In2Surrey does list it)
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you are eligible for a 16-19 bursary
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you live in a POLAR4 quintile 2 area
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you live in an IMD quintile 2 area
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you are a young carer or care for a relative with a disability, illness, mental health condition or addiction
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you are a refugee with indefinite leave to remain in the UK
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you have a disability or long-term health condition
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you have a parent or carer who has served in the UK Armed Forces or as a Reservist
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you are from a Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Showperson or Boater community
In2Surrey (apply; state school students): you are a mature or adult learner aged 21 or over when you start
In2Surrey: you have previously completed a Surrey Scholars activity (the Year 12 summer schools are part of Surrey Scholars)

contextual.rulesText: Automatic contextual offers are for UK home students: the page says that where an applicant meets one or more of its criteria (POLAR4 quintile 1, IMD quintile 1, care experience, free school meals, estranged) the application is considered under contextual admissions, and you must still meet the standard admissions requirements. Most applicants then get a reduced offer. If you don't qualify automatically, In2Surrey lets state school students who meet one of its criteria apply for an offer typically one grade lower. Criteria and postcode datasets can change each year (the details above are for 2027/28 entry).

source.evidence: you will receive a contextual offer that is typically two A-level grades or one BTEC grade or equivalent lower than the published grade for the programme you are applying for

programmes.name: In2Surrey
programmes.summary: Surrey's contextual admissions and transition scheme: if you don't get an automatic contextual offer but meet one of its criteria you can apply for an offer typically one A-level grade lower, plus online mentoring.
programmes.whoCanApply: UK students at a state school who meet at least one In2Surrey criterion, for example a 16-19 bursary, young carer, a POLAR4 or IMD quintile 2 area, a disability or long-term health condition, or having completed a Surrey Scholars activity.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: You attend a state school and meet one of: eligible for a 16-19 bursary; refugee with indefinite leave to remain in the UK; from a Gypsy, Roma, Irish Traveller, Showperson or Boater community; young carer; disability or long-term health condition; parent or carer who has served in the UK Armed Forces or as a Reservist; mature learner aged 21 or over; IMD quintile 2 postcode; POLAR4 quintile 2 postcode. People who have previously completed a Surrey Scholars activity are also eligible.
benefits: Offer typically one A-level grade (or equivalent) lower than the published grade; subject requirements are not reduced
Online mentoring with a current Surrey student
In2Surrey Transition Programme from June to October if Surrey is your firm choice

programmes.name: Surrey Year 12 Residential Summer School (Business strand)
programmes.summary: A free 4-day, 3-night residential at Surrey with sample lectures, workshops, research projects, sports tasters and evening socials; the 2026 subject strands were Business, Engineering Sciences and Veterinary Medicine.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students from groups under-represented in higher education who attend a non-selective state school or college in the UK and meet at least one of the listed criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Year 12 at a non-selective UK state school or college, and at least one of: POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2; IMD quintile 1 or 2; TUNDRA LSOA quintile 1 or 2; free school meals in the last six years; 16-19 bursary (or equivalent); care experienced; diagnosed disability or long-term health condition; young carer; forced migrant (for example refugee or asylum seeker); estranged from family; parent or carer who has served in the armed forces or reserves; Black, Asian or minority ethnic background; Gypsy, Roma or Traveller community; significant disruption due to illness or personal circumstance. Places depend on meeting the criteria and on the capacity of your chosen strand.
benefits: Overnight accommodation and three meals a day

notes: All course details are for 2027 entry (September 2027 start); Surrey hasn't published 2028 entry requirements yet.
No admissions test is listed on any of these course pages, and Surrey is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry.

On Economics, Economics and Finance and Business Economics and Data Analytics the offer drops from AAB to ABB if you take A-level Maths or A-level Economics (it can't be combined with other grade reductions such as the EPQ, contextual or In2Surrey).
Economics, Economics and Finance, Business Economics and Data Analytics and Economics and Mathematics share the same first year, so you can switch between them after year 1 (the course pages say so).

Each course also has a version with a Professional Training placement year (own UCAS code) and, for most, a foundation year (typical offer CCC, own UCAS code); the placement year fee is about 20% of the normal fee.

Surrey Scholars is Surrey's Years 9 to 13 outreach programme; the Year 12 summer schools are part of it. Its Chemistry, Computer Science and Health Sciences taster days are for other subjects and are not recorded.

Not included: Financial Mathematics, Politics, Law with Business and the other Business Management variants. Contextual criteria and offer reductions described are for 2027/28 entry; Surrey says the datasets change each year.
